display.purpose: The Hot Shop Atlas wordmark only; 22px on phones.

headline.purpose: Studio name in the detail view.

title.purpose: Studio names in chart rows (15.5px on phones); link rows use 800 at 16px.

label.purpose: Filter labels, sort, spec terms, chips, status; sentence case.

code.purpose: Chart numbers (HS-027) in rows and band tags; 13px for counts and distances.

code-small.purpose: Family counts on tabs, pin codes, URLs on link rows.

shadows.name: pin-lift
shadows.purpose: Map pins only; separates swatch pins from tiles.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Phone bottom sheet over the map.

shadows.name: chip-inset
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: draws the printed-chip margin and ink ring on row swatches (14px/15px on the detail band).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: All structural motion: row flood, family cap growth, pin scale, sheet height, filter chevron.

motion.name: flood
motion.purpose: Signature: rod colour sweeps left-to-right across the chosen row before the detail opens.

motion.name: sheet
motion.purpose: Phone bottom sheet between peek, half and full.

motion.name: family-cap
motion.purpose: Family tab colour cap grows 8px to 11px on hover and when pressed.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disables sheet, pin, flood and family-cap transitions.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: full-screen map with directory as a bottom sheet (peek 176px, half 52dvh, full 90dvh).

baseMap.attribution: OpenStreetMap attribution stays visible on a 92% chart-white strip.

variants.note: Shipped defaults are the data-* values on <html>: palette=chart, font=schibsted, density=regular, swatch=chip, map=grey, pin=code. tweaks.js (visible only with ?tweak) switches these sanctioned alternates.

components.css: :host{--paper:#fbfbf8;--paper-2:#f1f1ec;--ink:#14130f;--ink-2:#4a4840;--rule:#14130f;--t-hot:#e4572e;--t-flame:#0f7fa8;--t-kiln:#7a3fa0;--t-neon:#f2b705;--t-mixed:#4f8a3c;--sans:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'Chivo Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--ease:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} .ds-search{display:flex;gap:8px;padding:14px 24px;background:var(--paper);border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);} .ds-input{flex:1;min-width:0;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:0;padding:10px 12px;font:400 16px var(--sans);} .ds-input::placeholder{color:#6d6a60;} .ds-input:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:2px;} .ds-search-btn{background:var(--ink);color:#fff;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:0;padding:10px 14px;font:700 15px var(--sans);cursor:pointer;} .ds-search-btn:hover{background:#33312a;}

components.css: :host{--paper:#fbfbf8;--paper-2:#f1f1ec;--ink:#14130f;--ink-2:#4a4840;--rule:#14130f;--t-hot:#e4572e;--t-flame:#0f7fa8;--t-kiln:#7a3fa0;--t-neon:#f2b705;--t-mixed:#4f8a3c;--sans:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'Chivo Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--ease:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} .ds-fams{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr);border:1px solid var(--rule);max-width:520px;} .ds-fam{position:relative;border:0;border-right:1px solid var(--rule);background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);padding:18px 4px 10px;font:700 13px/1.15 var(--sans);cursor:pointer;} .ds-fam:last-child{border-right:0;} .ds-fam::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:0;height:8px;background:var(--c);transition:height .25s var(--ease);} .ds-fam span{display:block;font:500 12px var(--mono);color:var(--ink-2);margin-top:3px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;} .ds-fam:hover::before{height:11px;} .ds-fam[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--ink);color:#fff;} .ds-fam[aria-pressed="true"] span{color:#cfcdc4;} .ds-fam[aria-pressed="true"]::before{height:11px;} .ds-fam:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:-3px;}

components.css: :host{--paper:#fbfbf8;--paper-2:#f1f1ec;--ink:#14130f;--ink-2:#4a4840;--rule:#14130f;--t-hot:#e4572e;--t-flame:#0f7fa8;--t-kiln:#7a3fa0;--t-neon:#f2b705;--t-mixed:#4f8a3c;--sans:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'Chivo Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--ease:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} .ds-list{max-width:520px;border-top:1px solid var(--rule);} .ds-row{position:relative;isolation:isolate;display:grid;grid-template-columns:72px 92px 1fr;align-items:stretch;width:100%;min-height:68px;padding:0;text-align:left;background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);border:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);cursor:pointer;} .ds-sw{background:var(--c);border-right:1px solid var(--rule);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 9px var(--paper),inset 0 0 0 10px var(--ink);} .ds-sw.ds-approx{background:repeating-linear-gradient(135deg,var(--c) 0 6px,transparent 6px 12px),var(--paper);} .ds-code{display:grid;place-items:center;font:700 14px var(--mono);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;border-right:1px solid var(--rule);} .ds-txt{padding:12px 16px;display:grid;align-content:center;gap:2px;min-width:0;} .ds-name{font:800 16.5px/1.2 var(--sans);} .ds-meta{font:400 13px var(--sans);color:var(--ink-2);} .ds-row::before{content:"";position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:-1;background:var(--c);clip-path:inset(0 100% 0 0);transition:clip-path .3s var(--ease);} .ds-row:hover{background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--c) 10%,var(--paper));} .ds-row:active::before{clip-path:inset(0 0 0 0);} .ds-row.ds-light:active{color:#fff;} .ds-row.ds-light:active .ds-meta{color:rgba(255,255,255,.85);} .ds-row:active .ds-code,.ds-row:active .ds-sw{border-color:transparent;box-shadow:none;} .ds-row:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:-3px;}

narrative.overview:
The directory is printed like a glass manufacturer's rod chart (the Reichenbach or Kugler bar card a glassblower keeps by the bench). Every studio is a flat, coded swatch on chart-white paper, ruled off from its neighbours with 1px ink lines. A working glassblower should read it the way they read a colour chart: family colour first, code second, name third. It deliberately refuses the default finder of rounded result cards floating beside a map.

The surface is dense, flat and square. Hierarchy comes from weight, ink rules and colour fields rather than containers or elevation. Type is a single grotesque at heavy weights for names, with a mono reserved for anything that is counted or coded (chart numbers, totals, distances, URLs). The base map is quietened to grey so the five rod colours are the only saturated thing on screen. Motion is short and purposeful: the signature is a colour flood across the chosen row.

The shipped default is the set of `data-*` values on `<html>`: Chart palette, Schibsted headings, Regular rows, Chip swatches, Soft-grey map, type-code pins. A developer-only options panel (`?tweak`) can switch to the sanctioned variants listed in the sidecar; visitors never see it.
keyCharacteristics: Chart-white ground, ink text, 1px ink rules between every band and row.
Five rod colours, one per studio family, carried by swatches, bands, pins and the family filter.
Every colour is paired with a text code (HS, FW, KG, NE, MX, and HS-027 style chart numbers).
Square corners everywhere; no cards, no radius.
Schibsted Grotesk for words, Chivo Mono for codes and counts.
Desaturated base map; colour lives on the swatches, not the tiles.

rules.name: The Rods Are Families Rule
rules.body: The five rod colours mean studio type and nothing else (the two documented exceptions are the active Near me button and text selection). Never use a rod colour for decoration, emphasis or brand.

rules.name: The Code Carries Type Rule
rules.body: A rod colour never appears without its text code nearby: swatch beside a chart number, pin carrying HS/FW/KG/NE/MX, band carrying its HS-032 tag, family tab carrying its code and count. Colour must never be the only way to tell types apart.

rules.name: The Quiet Map Rule
rules.body: Map tiles are filtered to grey (grayscale 0.7, slight contrast and brightness lift) so the pins are the only saturated marks on the map.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Numbers Rule
rules.body: Chivo Mono sets only codes, counts, distances and URLs. Names, labels and prose are always Schibsted.

rules.name: The No Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case at 600-700 weight; the build uses no letter-spaced uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Flat Chart Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the directory column casts a shadow. Shadows belong only to marks and sheets that sit over the map.

dos: **Do** rule every band, row and cell with a 1px ink line; the rules are the structure.
**Do** pair every rod colour with its text code (HS, FW, KG, NE, MX or the full HS-027 number).
**Do** keep all corners square (0px), including third-party map controls.
**Do** set codes, counts, distances and URLs in Chivo Mono with tabular figures, and everything else in Schibsted Grotesk.
**Do** mark city-level locations with the diagonal hatch (swatches, bands) or dashed border (pins), never with an exact-looking solid mark.
**Do** keep the base map desaturated so rod colours are the only saturated marks.
**Do** put white text on flame and kiln, and ink text on hot, neon and mixed.
**Do** honour reduced motion: the flood, family caps, pins and sheet stop animating.
donts: **Don't** use rounded corners or soft cards anywhere in the directory.
**Don't** fake glass lighting on swatches (no glossy highlights, specular gradients or translucency); swatches are flat printed chips. The approximate-location hatch is the only patterned fill.
**Don't** cast shadows inside the directory column; shadows are reserved for pins, clusters and the phone sheet over the map.
**Don't** use a rod colour for anything except its studio family (beyond the active Near me state and text selection).
**Don't** add studio images, logos or decorative illustration; the swatches are the imagery.
**Don't** ship the colour-only square pin variant as the default; it drops the type code that keeps families legible without colour.
